evidence: The version lives in both marketplace.json plugins[0].version and plugin.json version, and TestClaudeMarketplaceListsPlugin compared only name/source; e9d2601 adds TestClaudeMarketplaceVersionMatchesPlugin with an absence arm so two empty strings cannot agree. Both manifests are read independently by Claude Code, so a guarded duplicate rather than derivation is a defensible reading of the law.
guidance_note: When a PR bumps a fact that is stored in two published files, add the equality test in the same PR rather than relying on a hand-synced bump.

evidence: The round-0 hunk ends the 'Your PRs elsewhere' arm at 'is yours to wrap up.' with no action, while the sibling 'This branch' arm names address-pr-reviews and 'Working the ticket'; the agent admits 'I wrote yours to wrap up and then never said what wrapping up consists of'.
guidance_note: When writing parallel arms of a procedure, check each arm ends in the same concrete next action as its sibling before pushing.

evidence: The agent ran the command and got '* links-workflow-p0dw' and '  remotes/origin/links-workflow-p0dw' - one branch, two decorated lines - confirming 'If it names a branch, check that one out' was not executable; e9d2601 adds --format and per-shape dispositions including git checkout -b <name> origin/<name>.
guidance_note: When writing a command into a procedure, run it in every shape the procedure claims to handle (local, remote-only, both) and write a disposition for each output shape, not just the one you tested.

evidence: The round-0 text conditioned orphan-pulling on 'when this checkout holds nothing' with no command; the reviewer's proposed lit backlog check is undercut by the agent's quoted store.go comment that a claimant is the (assignee, checkout) pair and lit backlog's own text 'only lit next routes by claim', so routing through lit next first is the sounder fix.
guidance_note: When a procedure branches on a fact, name the command that owns that fact; if only the router owns it, route through the router instead of asking the reader to infer state.

evidence: The self-flag on the 'This branch' path is real, but the reviewer's suggested select(.headRefName != current branch) was adopted verbatim even though step 2 runs before step 3's trunk switch, so on the pull-new-work path it hides the previous ticket's PR - exactly what F10 found and the agent conceded ('excluding whatever branch is checked out right now is wrong').
guidance_note: Before adopting a reviewer's filter, trace it through every arrival path that reaches the step, including where HEAD is at that point in the step order, and key the exclusion on the identity of the work (ticket id) rather than on ambient state.

evidence: Flag is a false positive: 'take the ticket id from its branch name' is already in the round-0 text (F2's hunk), and e9d2601 only split the paragraph; a shared @me account can return hand-cut branches with no id, which the text gave no disposition for, and f289e21 adds 'Leave it where it is.'
guidance_note: When a procedure extracts a field from external input, write the disposition for input where the field is absent in the same pass.

evidence: e9d2601 (F3's fix) added --format and itself named '+ for one checked out in another worktree' as a decoration being discarded, yet enumerated four outcome bullets with no worktree-held case; the agent reproduced 'fatal: ... is already used by worktree at ...' in its own worktree session.
guidance_note: When a fix deliberately discards information (here the + decoration), enumerate what that information signalled and add the failure it would have warned of to the outcome list.

evidence: Flag is a false positive: the sentence 'Plain ticket id, no slug - that is what makes the next session's search find it' is untouched by e9d2601 (its hunk shows no change there) and f289e21 replaces it, so it was in the original PR alongside the '*<ticket-id>*' glob that matches slugs and disproves it.
guidance_note: When justifying a convention, check the stated reason against the mechanism written in the same section; a substring glob two paragraphs up already refuted this one.

evidence: e9d2601 (F4's fix) introduced 'let what lit next actually said decide which of these you are in' over two bullets; the agent confirmed NoWork.Error() has a second shape 'no ready work - the backlog is not empty, but nothing in it is startable here', so the enumeration was incomplete.
guidance_note: When a fix routes on another command's outputs, enumerate that command's output type from source (every Error() branch) before writing the bullets, and do not assert exhaustiveness until you have.

evidence: e9d2601's select(.headRefName != $(git branch --show-current)) runs at step 2 before step 3 switches to trunk, so on the pull-new-work path it filters out the previous ticket's still-open PR; the agent took the reviewer's second option (key on ticket id) and verified #521 stays visible when working a different ticket.
guidance_note: When adding an exclusion to a check, test it on the arrival path where the excluded thing is not the current work, not only on the path that motivated the exclusion.

evidence: f289e21 (F9's fix) rewrote the third bullet as the literal-looking 'no ready work in <your epic>', but the agent-quoted Exhausted.Error() uses scope 'epic(s) <ids>' or 'your claimed lane(s)' and a tail that may be 'nothing else is queued behind what's already in progress', so the quote matched only one of four shapes.
guidance_note: When quoting a program's output as a match key, copy every format branch of the producing function rather than paraphrasing one into a template that looks literal.

evidence: The query returns a list, but the wrap-up procedure e9d2601 wrote for F2 is singular throughout ('check that branch out... Finish it before you pull anything new'), and those are the sentences the reviewer cites; 35b8a28 makes it 'Classify the whole list' and 'Every lane nobody holds'. The flag names f289e21, which only added the no-ticket-id paragraph; the singular disposition traces to F2's fix.
guidance_note: When writing the action for a query that returns a list, write it as a loop over every row and state the completion condition, not as handling for one row.

evidence: f289e21 (F10's fix) replaced exact equality with startswith("<ticket-id>") and added 'never a real overlap silently swallowed'; the agent confirmed Mint widens from MinHashLength 3 with taken() testing exact strings only, and reproduced startswith("links-workflow-abc") dropping links-workflow-abcd.
guidance_note: When replacing an exact match with a prefix match on identifiers, check whether one valid id can be a prefix of another before writing any safety claim about the filter.

evidence: 35b8a28 (F13's fix) interpolated the id into test("^<ticket-id>($|[_/])") even though the agent's own F13 reply stated ids use '[a-z0-9.-]'; the agent reproduced h2rgX1 being dropped and replaced the regex with literal == / startswith(id+"_") / startswith(id+"/") rather than the reviewer's escaping, which avoids relying on hand-escaping a pasted placeholder.
guidance_note: When interpolating a value into a regex, check the value's character set for metacharacters - here the agent had already listed '.' in the id alphabet - and prefer literal string comparison when the match is meant to be literal.

evidence: Duplicate of F14 from a parallel sweep: same unescaped '.' in test("^<ticket-id>($|[_/])") introduced by 35b8a28, citing ChildNamespace minting parentID + "."; the agent answered both threads with the one literal-comparison fix in 84ffb90.

Flag is a false positive: all three gh pr list invocations lacked --limit since round 0 (the F2/F5 hunks show them), and 35b8a28 did not touch that; the agent confirmed 'gh pr list --help' gives '--limit int ... (default 30)', so the overlap check silently truncated past 30 open PRs.
guidance_note: When writing a list command into a procedure that must see the whole set, check its default page size and pass an explicit limit.

narrative: A skill-text PR in which 10 of 16 findings were raised against the agent's own review fixes. The longest chain is the overlap-check filter: the reviewer's suggested current-branch exclusion (F5) hid the previous ticket's PR (F10), the ticket-id startswith fix swallowed longer ids (F13), and the anchored regex then widened on '.' in child ids (F14/F15) until literal comparison ended it. A second chain repeatedly mis-enumerated lit next's empty-handed outputs (F4 -> F9 -> F11). Round 1 and round 3 each also carried findings present since round 0 (F6, F8, F16); round 2 consisted only of fix-caused findings, so 1 avoidable round is a floor.
guidance_observations: Every fix to the overlap filter was verified only on the motivating case; testing each version against adversarial branch names (other arrival paths, prefix-extending ids, ids containing '.') would have collapsed four rounds into one.

The agent did read lit's source to verify findings, but only after the reviewer pointed there; reading next_route.go's full Error() branches when first writing the routing bullets would have prevented F9 and F11.
The agent's F13 reply listed '.' in the id alphabet and still put the id into a regex in the same commit - a stated fact was not checked against the fix being written alongside it.
